claim: The Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI), a utility-industry research body, measured radio-frequency emissions from an Itron smart meter in its December 2010 report (product 1021126) and concluded that exposure falls off rapidly with distance, that the meters transmit only a small fraction of the time, and that levels stay well below the U.S. FCC's maximum permissible exposure (MPE) — an industry white paper summarizing the measurements put exposure through a wall at roughly 0.01% of the FCC limit and reported exposure 'well below FCC standard limits' even in close proximity. The report expresses its results as percentages of the FCC MPE, not as a fixed µW/cm² field value; a '7.93 µW/cm²' figure attributed to it corresponds to a percent-of-limit worst-case (radio forced to transmit continuously), not a measured power density, and understates the true peak. The conclusion is contested: Sage Associates — the group that also edited the BioInitiative Report — argued in a 2011 response that EPRI did not model banks of multiple meters at high duty cycle, which under the FCC's own OET-65 rules could approach or exceed the public limit in worst-case assumptions.

notes: Group A / context record from capture DamkicUoJo8. Documents what the EPRI Itron report actually concluded (emissions well below FCC MPE at normal distances; meters duty-cycle a small fraction of the time) and the named counter-position (Sage Associates 2011, multi-meter high-duty worst case under OET-65). The clip's 'EPRI measured a meter at up to 7.93 µW/cm²' is the misread: 7.93 is a percent-of-MPE value, not a measured µW/cm² power density (per subagent trace; actual near-field peak estimates are higher, ~48-79 µW/cm², but the report frames everything as % of the FCC limit and predicts no violations). Presented two-sided per the 'reader chooses' ethos — EPRI is industry-funded, Sage is the BioInitiative editor; neither is a neutral regulator. Pairs with [[2017-emf-exposure-limits-001]] and [[2017-emf-bioeffect-chart-001]]. Not an EFTA-corpus subject.
